newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ok Tedi copper mine still in grip of drought.
newsitem.headline: Ok Tedi copper mine still in grip of drought.

text.p: Drought continued to leave mining at a standstill at the Ok Tedi copper and gold mine in Papua New Guinea, the mine's operator, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Monday.
"There was no rain over the weekend, so there has been no change," a BHP spokesman told Reuters from Port Moresby.

BHP has maintained open communications with customers who buy the mine's estimated 60,000 tonnes of copper concentrates a month since low water levels on the Fly River forced the suspension of barge transport of the concentrates, he said.
"There are no customers who have outstanding shipments they are waiting on," the spokesman said.

Ok Tedi has long-term supply contracts with Germany's Norddeutsche Affinerie, Finland's Outokumpu Oy, Philippines Associated Smelting and Refining Corp (PASAR), South Korea's LG Metals Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd and the Japanese Smelter Pool which consists of seven Japanese smelters. The mine, located in PNG's Western Province, was forced about a week ago to shut the second of two semi-autogenous grinding (SAG) mills after reviewing supplies of diesel fuel.
The mine's other SAG mill was shut the preceding week.
Activities at the mine are continuing to focus on removal of waste and overburden to expose the ore in preparation for a return to mining once the rains come, the spokesman said.
Concentrates are normally barged to a silo-ship at the mouth of the Fly River for transshipment to bulk carriers.
BHP owns 52.6 percent of the mine. The other partners are Canada's Inmet Mining Corp with 17.4 percent and the PNG government, which holds the rest.
